title: Pop Stretch: Grunge, Britpop, EDM & Streaming

walkthroughs.body_html:
Grunge arrived in 1991 with Nirvana's Nevermind. It mixed punk rawness with metal heaviness — quiet verses, loud distorted choruses.

Across the Atlantic in 1994, Britpop celebrated British identity. Oasis and Blur battled for the No.1 spot in 1995, drawing on Beatles-style hooks and 60s mod culture.

EDM covers many sub-genres — house (~120 BPM), techno, trance (~140 BPM), dubstep (~140 BPM, half-time feel), drum & bass (~175 BPM).

Structure often follows intro – build-up – drop – breakdown – build – drop. The drop is the explosive climax where the beat hits hardest.

Streaming (Spotify launched 2008, Apple Music 2015) replaced album sales as the main revenue. Songs got shorter, with hooks in the first 30 seconds to fight 'skip rates'.

Bedroom producers using a DAW (Ableton, Logic, FL Studio) can now reach global audiences via TikTok and streaming algorithms — no record label needed.
